post.linkedin_text:
Is your website built for phones, or does it just open on one? Those are two very different things.
A mobile friendly website is made for a thumb and a small screen first. Not shrunk down from a laptop design.

Here's why it matters. When someone finds you on Instagram or through a Meta ad, they tap your link inside the app. So your site opens on a phone. That's the first impression.

But most of us design and check our websites on a laptop. So the problems don't show up for us. They only show up for the customer.

The 3 mistakes I'd check first:
1. Text and buttons so small that people have to pinch and zoom.
2. The "Book now" or WhatsApp button sits four scrolls down instead of near the top.
3. Heavy images that load fast on office wifi but crawl on mobile data.

A simple example: a clinic website with a long intro and the contact button at the very bottom. On a phone, a patient has to dig for it. Put the clinic name, what you treat and one clear button on the first screen, and booking becomes easy.

So a mobile friendly website isn't a fancy extra. It's where your Instagram and ad visitors actually land.

Swipe through for each fix 👇

Quick test: open your own site on your phone today, the way a customer would.

Which one is your site guilty of: 1, 2 or 3?

#WebDesign #SmallBusiness #DigitalMarketing

linkedin_carousel.title: Mobile Friendly Website: 3 Mistakes to Fix

slides.heading: Your visitors are on a phone
slides.body: Someone taps your link on Instagram or a Meta ad. Your website opens inside the app, on a small screen. That's the first impression.

slides.heading: Mistake 1: tiny text and buttons
slides.body: If people have to pinch and zoom to read or tap, most just go back. Keep text easy to read and buttons big enough for a thumb.

slides.heading: Mistake 2: the button is too far down
slides.body: On a laptop your Book now button sits on screen. On a phone it can end up four scrolls down. Put one clear action near the top.

slides.heading: Mistake 3: slow, heavy pages
slides.body: Big images look great on office wifi. On mobile data they take ages to load. Compress images and cut what isn't needed.

slides.heading: Example: a clinic website
slides.body: Before: long intro, contact button at the bottom. After: clinic name, what you treat and a WhatsApp button, all on the first screen.

linkedin_carousel.closing_heading: Check it on your own phone
